transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
President Trump says he is open to working with Democrats
on one issue impacting Americans,
high credit card interest rates.
NPR's Chantalice Duster has the story.
- President Trump says he is open to working with Democrats
in the new Congress to cap credit card interest rates.
Trump has pushed for a 10% cap.
In an interview with Fox News on Saturday,
the president said credit card companies
are getting too much.
- Some people say it's not free enterprise,
but what's free enterprise?
When you're sitting home and you get a bill
that some guy set up in an office on parking avenue,
and they said, "Let's charge a fee that's to high."
So I'm all for that.
- Interest rates for credit cards are nearly 22%.
Democrats, including Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren
have said they are ready to work with Trump
to cap interest rates.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
- About 81 million people are expected to travel
over Thanksgiving week, but in California,
where high tides and heavy rains are forecast,
one mayor is urging residents to consider staying home.
And Pierre's Ava Berger reports.
- As Americans set their minds on pumpkin pie
and cranberry sauce, the weather is not cooperating.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Laurie said next week,
the city is expecting extreme high tides and rain.
- I'm going to ask you all to consider not traveling
unless it is absolutely essential starting Monday afternoon
and going into Wednesday afternoon.
- Two atmospheric rivers, which are long bands
of water vapor that dump rain on certain areas,
will hover over Northern California
and the Pacific Northwest.
On the Eastern seaboard, a storm is forecasted
to move through the Carolinas into New England.
Meteorologists say that storm won't be as bad
as the one in California, but during a busy travel week,
any challenging weather can cause delays.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
- In Johannesburg, South Africa,
hundreds of women demonstrators called for urgent action
against gender-based violence.
Quarterly police statistics this week
showed nearly 600 women were murdered in South Africa
over three months, and Pierre's Kate Bartlett has more.
- The protesters marched through Johannesburg,
parading an empty coffin,
and then conducted a 15-minute lion.
They all lay flat to represent the grim statistic
that 15 women are killed daily in South Africa.
The protest comes a year after President Cyril Ramaphosa
called gender-based violence a national crisis.
But the women say not enough has been done.
Police statistics released this week showed 581 women
were killed between July and September,
and almost 10,000 reported being raped.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg.
- You're listening to NPR News in Washington.
The Kansas City Chiefs Wheelchair Football Team
has won its third straight national championship,
defeating the wheelchair Chicago Bears 20-7 in Kansas City.
Frank Morris of member station KCUR reports.
(crowd cheers)
- The win solidified the Chiefs spot
at the top of the USA Wheelchair Football League.
It was the Chiefs' third straight championship win
against their arch rival, the wheelchair Chicago Bears,
and it left Chiefs star quarterback, Matt Bolig,
feeling good about the year.
- Definitely enjoyed the season,
and we didn't go undefeated like we did last year,
but putting the three-peat on the,
is the cherry on top for sure, it was a lot of fun.
- The USA Wheelchair Football League is only six years old.
It's grown from four to 15 teams around the country,
most adopting the names of NFL teams,
and all but one hoping to knock the wheelchair chiefs
down a peg next year.
For NPR News, I'm Frank Morris in Kansas City.
- Bear has agreed to pay up to $7.25 billion
over the next two decades
to settle thousands of US claims
related to its weed killer, Roundup.
The settlement approved by a Missouri judge
covers people diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Participants could receive between 10,000 and $165,000.
Bear denies that Roundup causes cancer,
but sought a settlement amid growing litigation costs.
The settlement aims to resolve most remaining lawsuits,
as well as future claims from people exposed to Roundup
before the settlement was reached.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
This message comes from Angie.
Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years.
For everything from minor repairs to major remodels,
find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com
or on the Angie app.

topics.text: President Trump says he is open to working with Democrats on capping credit card interest rates
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie urges residents to avoid nonessential travel amid Thanksgiving storms and high tides
Hundreds of women protest gender-based violence in Johannesburg, citing 581 women killed in three months
Kansas City Chiefs win third straight USA Wheelchair Football League championship over Chicago Bears
Bayer agrees to pay up to $7.25 billion to settle Roundup weed killer cancer claims
